_comment: Which CLI a CLI-example check run is against (PLAN section 7.12): the
released CLI for the public site, the candidate channel for the candidate
build.
HOW THE METADATA REACHES CI. kubenest-cli's cmd/gen-command-metadata emits
the command tree as JSON and .github/workflows/build.yml attaches it to
every release as command-metadata.json, so a docs run never builds Go.
cli-metadata/command-metadata.json is the COMMITTED snapshot the workflows
read, which is what makes the docs deploy depend on this repository only --
deploy.yml's own rule, after the Helm-values guard once failed closed on a
private checkout. It was generated from kubenest-cli's tree at the v2.0.0
release (whose pkg/cmd differs from that tree only by the
kubenest.io/unavailable annotation this guard reads) because v2.0.0's
release carries no such asset: the asset exists from the NEXT tag onward,
and ci.yml fetches it when it does.
cli-metadata/command-metadata.json is kept honest by
kubenest-cli/cmd/gen-command-metadata/main_test.go, which regenerates the
tree and fails when the committed copy's commands no longer match (it skips
where the umbrella workspace is not checked out beside the CLI, the same
rule pkg/bundles' contract test follows).
MOVING THE TARGET RELEASE IS A REVIEW OBLIGATION. Nothing checks that
public_site.release is the version docs.kubenest.io should document; a
release that is promoted without bumping it is checked against the wrong
tree, and the pages do not fail.
